common_name: Ruby Glow Pentas (Old-Fashioned Tall Red Egyptian Star Cluster)

planting.note: Set out transplants after all danger of frost has passed and soil has warmed, since this heirloom selection resents cool, wet conditions; established plants in zone 9b and warmer often return from the roots after a mild winter.

directions: Unlike the compact bedding series bred for uniformity, Ruby Glow keeps the looser, taller habit and heavier nectar production of older-style pentas, making it a favorite with butterfly gardeners rather than container growers. Plant in fertile, well-drained soil and allow it room to grow into a rounded, multi-stemmed shrublet rather than crowding it as a dwarf bedding plant. Pinch young plants once to encourage branching, then let the glowing red flower domes develop through summer with only occasional deadheading. In frost-free areas it becomes a semi-woody perennial that can be cut back hard in late winter to renew growth for the coming season.

common_name: Graffiti Lipstick Pentas (Red with White Eye Compact Bedding Pentas)

planting.note: Transplant into warm garden soil or containers once nights stay reliably above 50°F; this seed-series color holds its bicolor pattern best in full sun and consistent heat.

directions: Graffiti Lipstick pairs a vivid red star-shaped corolla with a small white eye at the center of each floret, giving the flower domes a speckled, two-tone look from a distance. It stays tight and mounded like the rest of the Graffiti series, so it holds its shape in the front of a border or a mixed container without staking or shearing. Feed lightly through the growing season to sustain the dense, continuous flush of bloom clusters, and remove spent flower heads on a mature planting to keep new buds forming. Full sun and reliable heat bring out the sharpest contrast between the red petals and white centers.

common_name: Graffiti White Pentas (Compact White-Flowered Bedding Pentas)

planting.note: Set out after the last frost date into well-drained beds or containers; white-flowered pentas shows best against darker foliage neighbors and brightens plantings viewed in the evening.

directions: Graffiti White forms the same tight, uniform mound as its series-mates but carries pure white flower clusters that stand out sharply against the dark green foliage. It is a strong nighttime and moth-garden performer, since the pale flowers remain visible well after other colors fade into the dusk. Plant in full sun with even moisture for the heaviest bloom count, and avoid overhead watering late in the day, which can spot the petals. Deadheading is rarely necessary on younger plants, but shearing lightly midseason keeps a mature planting dense and floriferous into fall.

common_name: Graffiti Lavender Pink Pentas (Compact Lavender-Pink Bedding Pentas)

planting.note: Move transplants outdoors once soil has warmed after the last frost; this soft lavender-pink shade combines easily with both cool and warm color schemes in mixed beds and containers.

directions: This Graffiti color strain produces soft lavender-pink flower domes on the same compact, well-branched framework shared across the series, making it easy to mix with Graffiti Red or White for a uniform-height bedding display. Grow in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil, and keep plants evenly watered during the hottest stretches of summer to prevent the flower clusters from fading or bleaching. Light monthly feeding sustains the nonstop bloom cycle from planting through the first fall frost. Because the plants stay dense and low, they need no pinching to remain full and tidy in beds or containers.

common_name: Lucky Star Pentas (Compact Texas Superstar Star-Cluster Pentas Series)

planting.note: Transplant after soil has warmed following the last frost; this dwarf seed series was bred and trialed specifically for heat and humidity tolerance across the Gulf South, so it can go into beds and containers as soon as nights are reliably warm.

directions: Lucky Star is a dwarf seed-grown pentas series named a Texas Superstar and Louisiana Super Plant for its compact habit and heavy bloom output across Dark Red, Deep Pink, Pink, Lavender, Violet, Lipstick, and White Improved color selections. Plants stay noticeably shorter and tighter than older pentas types, so they hold up well in mass plantings and containers without flopping or stretching in summer heat. Grow in full sun in well-drained, fertile soil, and water regularly during establishment; once rooted in, the series tolerates the hot, humid summers of the Gulf Coast with minimal maintenance. Light feeding through the season keeps the dense flower clusters coming continuously and draws steady butterfly and hummingbird traffic.
sources: Texas Superstar Program, Texas A&M AgriLife Extension

common_name: Sunstar Pentas (Large-Flowered Proven Winners Star-Cluster Pentas Series)

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated transplants after the last frost once temperatures stay warm; the Sunstar series is bred for extra-large flower heads and benefits from full sun and steady warmth to size up quickly.

directions: Sunstar is a vegetatively propagated Proven Winners pentas series bred for unusually large, dense flower clusters in shades including Red II, Pink, and Rose, held above dark green foliage on plants that need no deadheading to rebloom continuously. Give it full sun and consistently moist, well-drained soil; the oversized flower domes draw heavy pollinator and hummingbird traffic all summer into fall. Because plants run somewhat larger and wider than seed-grown pentas series, allow extra spacing in beds and containers so the flower heads can fully expand without crowding neighbors. Regular light fertilizing through the growing season supports the heavier bloom load this series is bred to produce.
